groups.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed new cross-border drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia and its airports on October 7, 2026.

Houthi forces launched a ballistic missile and drone attack campaign targeting Riyadh, King Khalid International Airport, and Abqaiq oil facilities, resulting in interceptions, falling debris, infrastructure damage, and flight suspensions on October 8, 2026.
Falling shrapnel and debris from an intercepted ballistic missile over Riyadh caused material damage to a kindergarten and medical clinic complex on October 8, 2026.
The Arab coalition reported destroying a ballistic missile launcher platform used in attacks against Riyadh.
Turkey deployed drone operators, air defense systems, and technical military support to Saudi Arabia to counter Houthi threats.
The United States issued travel and security warnings for its citizens in Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks.
Regional bodies including the Muslim World League, GCC, and Arab League strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and civilian infrastructure.
Major international airlines such as Lufthansa, Air India, and IndiGo suspended or diverted flights to Riyadh following missile disruptions and security threats.
India formally condemned Houthi attacks targeting airports in Saudi Arabia.
The UN condemned Houthi drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi airports near Riyadh and Abha.
Regional sources reported that Saudi Arabia will not agree to a ceasefire with the Houthis until the Saudi-backed Yemeni government regains all lost territory.
The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones targeting Riyadh and Khamis Mushait on September 26, 2026.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan convened in Riyadh under the Mecca Agreement and activated collective defense and deterrence measures against Houthi threats.
Saudi Arabia deployed 100 fighter jets in Operation Dawn of Yemen to challenge Houthi control over the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Saudi Arabia requested air-defense support from France, Britain, Pakistan, and Egypt against Houthi attacks.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey announced plans to hold defense pact talks amid ongoing Houthi attacks.
Saudi Arabia condemned a terrorist attack in Dera Ismail Khan and expressed solidarity with Pakistan.
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia condemned a Houthi missile or drone attack on an electricity distribution station in Madinah on October 2, 2026.
Pakistan vowed to provide available means to defend Saudi Arabia if it faces threats from the Houthis.
Syrian President Sharaa visited Saudi Arabia for regional consultations, while Syria denied reports of deploying troops to Yemen.
The IDF shifted its forces in southern Lebanon toward a forward-defense posture and prepared positions for winter.
The Saudi energy minister stated that the East-West pipeline pumps 5.8 million barrels daily.
Italian KC-767A and C-130J aircraft appeared at Riyadh following an attack on Taif air base.
Pakistan reportedly retaliated against Houthi forces following a bombing at a Saudi base that killed Pakistani troops.
The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting and destroying multiple Houthi ballistic missiles and drones targeting Riyadh, Khamis Mushait, and other locations.
Saudi Arabia reported three people injured in attacks on its airports amid renewed fighting with Houthi forces.

Houthi forces launched a wave of missile and drone attacks targeting Riyadh International Airport, Abha Airport, Khamis Mushait air base, and Aramco facilities, accompanied by heavy clashes in Yemen on October 6-7, 2026.
